subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What recurring types of problems show up in these incident tickets?

judge.implied_focus: The nature/type of recurring problem in each incident ticket, characterized along a taxonomy of problem-defining facets (what kind of issue, how it fails, what it affects, and its scope).

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Classifies the problem domain (email, database, vpn, etc.), a core facet of 'what type of problem' and directly enables recurring-type analysis.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: Captures HOW the problem manifests (connection_failure, outage, access_denied), a distinct and highly relevant facet for typing recurring problems.

per_column.name: affected_component
per_column.rationale: Identifies the technical locus of the problem (server_side, remote_access, client_application), adding orthogonal structure to the problem taxonomy.

per_column.name: scope_context
per_column.rationale: Describes the breadth/context of impact (individual_user, production_environment, department), a coherent facet, though it overlaps somewhat with affected_component (remote_access appears in both).

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Constant 'true' for all 500 rows; it carries zero information and cannot differentiate recurring vs non-recurring problems, so it does not realise the focus despite its on-topic name.

per_column.name: resolution_same_day
per_column.rationale: A resolution/SLA attribute, not a facet of the problem TYPE; it drifts toward outcome/handling rather than the recurring-problem taxonomy the query asks for.

judge.rationale: The columns collectively centre on a coherent inferable focus: a multi-facet taxonomy of incident problem types (category x failure_mode x affected_component x scope). Four of six columns form a genuinely differentiated, non-trivial predictor/attribute set at a useful granularity that would let an analyst surface recurring problem clusters -- clearly beyond mechanical text metrics. This is actionable: an analyst can group and count these facets to identify dominant recurring problem types. Coherence and structure are dented by two weak columns: recurrence_signal is a constant with no discriminative value (vacuous), and resolution_same_day shifts to resolution/outcome rather than problem typing. There is also mild redundancy between affected_component and scope_context. Overall a solid but not clean realisation of focus inference.
